newsitem.title: USA: ESS Tech drops on Q2 warning, downgrades.
newsitem.headline: ESS Tech drops on Q2 warning, downgrades.

text.p: Shares of ESS Technology Inc dropped nearly six percent after the company warned it expects to see second quarter revenue growth of only 22 percent due to softer-than-expected demand for audio products.

ESS, which supplies mixed signal PC audio solutions that integrate essential audio components on a single chip, dropped 2 to 12-5/8. By mid-afternoon, more than 4.5 million shares changed hands, about four times ESS Technology's average daily trading volume.
Hambrecht & Quist and Volpe Brown Whelan & Co also downgraded the stock and trimmed their earnings expectations.
After the market closed on Thursday, ESS Technology also said the second quarter would be dampened by competitive pricing pressures in the audio and video CD markets.

"We anticipated this quarter might be difficult, because of historic slow seasonal demand and competitive price pressure and because it is a transition quarter to our new products for the second half of the year," said chief executive Fred Chan.
Ian Gilson, an analyst with Van Kasper & Co, said the market overreacted to ESS Technology's second quarter warning.
"It's a lower rate of growth, but it's still growth," Gilson said.
"Everyone, ESS and others, are facing a transition to new technology ... it's an industry problem that will sort itself out," Gilson said.

ESS Technology said it expected net sales for the second quarter, ending June 30, 1997, to be between $56 and $61 million and earnings between to be $0.16 and $0.19 per share before a one-time charge of $0.64 per share resulting from the acquisition of Platform Technologies Inc for 2.54 million shares of ESS common stock.
ESS earned $0.28 per share in the second quarter of 1996.
Volpe Brown said although ESS Technology's long-term fundamentals remain intact, downward pricing pressure will pressure the PC audio market for the rest of 1997.
Volpe Brown cut its 1997 earnings expectations to $1.30 a share from $1.70 a share and the 1998 estimate to $2.10 a share from $2.20 a share.
Hambrecht & Quist analyst Rob Chaplinsky also trimmed his 1997 earnings expectations to $1.24 a share from $1.60 a share and the 1998 estimate to $1.76 a share from $2.10 a share.
Other analysts cited ESS Technology's recent acquisition of Platform Technologies Inc as a positive move, saying it will help bolster development in PCI-based audio solutions.
Volpe Brown also said it expects the next generation VideoCD products to contribute "meaningfully to revenues in the second half of 1997 and 1998."
